newsitem.title: USA: Mead says lower prices, volumes hurt EPS.
newsitem.headline: Mead says lower prices, volumes hurt EPS.

text.p: Mead Corp said its second quarter earnings declined versus a year ago in its coated paper, paperboard and corrugating medium business segments but improved over the first quarter on seasonal increases in beverage packaging and school products.
Mead earned $0.90 per share on sales of $1.32 billion in the quarter versus $1.32 per share on $1.26 billion in sales last year.
The company cited lower prices for paper and corrugating medium, and decreased volume in the company's distribution business for the profit decline.
It noted, however, that prices strengthened near the end of the quarter for pulp, coated paper, and corrugating medium.

"We are encouraged by the strengthening prices we now see as a result of increased demand in pulp, coated paper and containerboard, and by the continued strength of our other value-added products," Steven Mason, Mead's chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.
